newsitem.title: USA: Equifax stockholder seeks company investigation.
newsitem.headline: Equifax stockholder seeks company investigation.

text.p: A dissident stockholder said Tuesday that he presented a formal request to Equifax Inc. seeking an independent investigation by its board into allegedly questionable practices at the Atlanta credit-reporting company.
John Phillips, whose company, Aristotle Publishing Inc., sued Equifax in December, said in a statement that the board of directors of Equifax had received his formal request.
Washington-based Aristotle Publishing filed a lawsuit in December alleging improper sales of restricted voter registration information by Equifax's CDB/Infotek unit.
Officials of Equifax, an Atlanta-based information services firm, were not immediately available to comment. Phillips was also not immediately available.

Phillips said in his statement that his request asked the company to determine why officers allegedly failed to detect the sale of data for illegal purposes at the time the CDB unit was acquired by Equifax.
It also asked the board to require officers to make full disclosure to shareholders and to government authorities, Phillips said.
He said he also demanded the board audit the use of all 2.5 billion of the unit's "public records" to insure its data offerings were in compliance with all applicable laws.
